description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Initial Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and a third unlabeled metric represented by a solid blue line with circle markers—across a range of initial confidence values from 0.86 to 1.00. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” is linearly scaled with tick marks at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also linearly scaled, with major gridlines at 0.2 intervals. The solid blue line with circle markers remains consistently high, hovering near 0.95 to 1.0 across all confidence levels, with small error bars indicating low variance. The green dashed line with square markers, labeled “Initial Accuracy,” starts at approximately 0.65 at 0.86 confidence, rises gradually to a peak near 0.92 at 0.95–0.96 confidence, then declines to about 0.75 at 1.00 confidence. The orange dashed line with diamond markers, labeled “Δ Accuracy,” begins at ~0.3 at 0.86 confidence, drops to near 0.05 around 0.93–0.95 confidence, then rises again to ~0.2 at 1.00 confidence, showing a U-shaped trend with larger error bars indicating higher variability, especially at the extremes. The plot visually suggests that while the unlabeled blue metric remains stable, both Initial Accuracy and Δ Accuracy exhibit non-monotonic behavior as initial confidence increases, with Δ Accuracy showing the most pronounced dip in the mid-range.
